gaps.text: In-line measurement of Product temperature at the measurement point with temperature sensor at the probe position

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (NIR reflection and MIR-ATR must look at the same measurement point, through a combined probe or two probes at one port, with the data normalised to a common time step. Start from one calibration per method, then fuse block-scaled spectra or per-method scores, and keep a separate calibration and diagnostics for each instrument. The combined model has to beat the best single method on independent runs, otherwise the extra instrument is not worth keeping.)

Any accuracy, detection limit or response-time figure for fat or protein in this product: the enquiry asks for earlier composition information, but no supplied source states such figures for an opaque, concentrated milk product.

items.finding: Temperature sensitivity of OH bands in aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR is a severe drawback, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For an opaque concentrated milk product, temperature at the measurement point may affect NIR/MIR spectra, so measuring or controlling temperature at the probe could be important for O2.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a review statement about aqueous solutions and tempered sample holders, not an in-line milk trial; transfer to a concentrated, opaque product and a process probe is uncertain.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E03 ¶12

items.finding: Temperature was varied along with acid concentrations and ionic strength to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests including temperature as a varied factor and possibly measuring it at the probe when building calibrations for O2.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The study is on reactive liquid-liquid extraction in lithium recycling, not milk, and does not describe an in-line temperature sensor at the probe.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E02 ¶19

items.finding: The Gerber method for fat in liquid milk has a rapid analysis time of approximately 5-10 min per sample.
items.how_it_applies: This gives a lab reference time for fat, which could inform the practical comparison experiment while retaining laboratory checks, but it is not an in-line figure for the customer's product.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The figure is for liquid milk and a manual butyrometric lab method, not an opaque concentrated milk product or a spectroscopy method.

citation.quote: The Gerber method offers several practical advantages for liquid milk analysis: (1) rapid analysis time (approximately 5-10 min per sample), (2) no requirement for drying or pre-extraction of the sample-directly applicable to liquid milk, (3) simple equipment and low cost, and (4) suitable for routine quality control in processing plants.
citation.label: E04 ¶35
